blocks.content: The Solar System consists of the Sun and the celestial bodies bound to it by gravity, including eight planets and their satellites.

rows: Few or no moons; no rings
Numerous moons; system of rings present

items: Venus and Uranus rotate from East to West (retrograde rotation), whereas all other planets rotate from West to East.
The Asteroid Belt is situated strictly between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
Mercury and Venus are the only two planets in the Solar System that have no natural moons.
Ganymede (Jupiter's moon) is larger than the planet Mercury and is the largest satellite in the Solar System.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Solar System comprises the Sun, eight major planets, dwarf planets, natural satellites, asteroids, comets, and meteoroids bound together by gravity.
Planets are divided into two main categories: Inner/Terrestrial planets (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars) and Outer/Jovian planets (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune).
Venus is the hottest planet due to an extreme runaway greenhouse effect caused by a dense carbon dioxide atmosphere, and is often called Earth's Twin.
The Asteroid Belt is a region located between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter, containing thousands of rocky bodies.
Jupiter has the fastest rotational period (~10 hours) and hosts Ganymede, the largest moon in the Solar System.
